blindSourceSummaries: A digital news outlet (February 2025): the legislature's women's and family committee unanimously approved a package of two 2023 bills that would prohibit entry to public restrooms designated for the sex assigned at birth (exceptions: custody, medical attention, accompanying a person under 12, an elderly or disabled person) and prohibit ambiguous bathroom signage; the package still required a plenary vote. Context: in July 2023 a complaint about gendered signage at the country's main international airport led to the signs being changed to inclusive labels. An activist notes no official statistics on trans violence in public restrooms exist, and enforcement would rest on individual security staff checking identity documents.

A university human-rights institute's bulletin (April 2025): in early April 2025 the legislature's plenary approved, waiving a second vote, a law strengthening protection of children and adolescents against sexual violations (merging two 2023 bills). A provision of the bill bans entry to and use of public restrooms for any person whose biological sex does not match the facility's designated sex, with narrow exceptions for accompaniment or assistance and legal or judicial mandates. The bulletin reads the provision as a direct violation of equality and non-discrimination (the constitution's equality clause and a regional human-rights convention, in line with the regional human-rights court's advisory opinion), and as validating stereotypes about trans people.

An LGBTI news outlet (July 2024) on the annual report of a university LGBTI rights observatory: 54 LGBTI homicides and 170 rights-violation cases between 2020 and 2023; more than half the homicide victims were trans women (30), then gay men (23) and one lesbian woman; yearly homicides 2020: 12 (8 trans women), 2021: 10, 2022: 13, 2023: 19 (12 trans women). Killings involved extreme cruelty (multiple gunshots, stabblings, throat-cuttings); rights violations peaked at 61 in 2020 (43 in 2022, 34 in 2023, 32 in 2021), trans women again the most affected. Includes testimony that in February 2023 an extortion gang abducted a 31-year-old sex worker in the capital's central area and killed her in a district on the outskirts with about 30 shots, a case of the sex-trade organised-crime violence the movement identifies as the main trans-femicide driver.
blindTangential: Community-justice assemblies hold dispute-resolution authority in parts of this state/province, and the constitution permits community justice within human-rights limits: a complaint — including one over gender expression — may be settled by a village assembly rather than in court. No trans-specific case documented; recorded as a structural caveat of the country-level research.
